aiTitle: Saturday Rush: The Wine Order and the Rota

message.content: Good morning. It’s Saturday, April 11th, 2026. I need to get my head straight before the lunch rush. Can you pull up the pending supplier orders for this week?

content.text: Good morning, Mateo. I have the dashboard ready. For the wine stock, you have a pending confirmation with Bodegas Turia for 24 bottles of their 2024 Albariño. The rest of your produce order from the central market is confirmed for delivery at 5 AM today. Do you want to adjust the wine order before I finalize it?

message.content: Yes, hold on. The Albariño is fine, but I need to swap the reds. We’re running low on the Tempranillo. Can you check if we can add ten more bottles from Bodegas Turia to that same invoice? I don’t want to pay for a second delivery fee.

content.text: I’ve checked Bodegas Turia’s current stock. They have the Tempranillo available. I’ve added 10 bottles to your existing draft order. The total has been updated. Shall I send the confirmation now?

message.content: Yes, send it. Now, switch to the staff rota. I have a feeling we’re going to be short on the dinner service. Check who is available for Saturday night.

content.text: Looking at the rota for Saturday, April 11th, 2026: You have Carlos and Elena scheduled for the morning prep. For the dinner shift, Marco is working, but his shift ends at 9 PM. You have a gap from 9 PM to closing. Sofia is off today, but she is available for an extra shift if you need her.

message.content: Sofia can stay until closing, but only if she gets double time. Please update her contract for tonight to reflect that. Also, I need to check the menu costing for the new paella variant we’re testing. The rice price went up again.

content.text: I’ve updated Sofia’s shift to include the overtime rate. Regarding the paella, I’ve recalculated the cost based on the latest rice supplier rates. The cost per portion has increased by 0.40 euros. To maintain your 30% food cost margin, you would need to increase the menu price from 18.00 to 19.50. Do you want to apply this change immediately?

message.content: 19.50 is too steep for a Saturday lunch. Let’s keep it at 18.50 for now and eat the margin hit for this week. I’ll review it next month. Now, check my license renewal status. I’m worried about the noise permit expiring.

content.text: Your noise permit for the restaurant location does not expire until October 2026, so you are safe for now. However, your general business operating license renewal is due next month. Would you like me to draft the email to the city council and prepare the required documents?

message.content: Yes, please draft it. And while you’re at it, check if there are any pending legal notices for Carmen. I know she’s busy with the custody schedule for Pablo, but I need to make sure she’s handled the paperwork. Her lawyer is Abogada Torres, right?

content.text: I have checked the legal directory. Abogada Torres is indeed Carmen’s regular lawyer. There are no pending urgent notices from her office requiring your immediate action, but I see a document scheduled for signature next Tuesday. I can remind you on Monday morning if you’d like.

message.content: Yes, remind me on Monday. I have to pick up Pablo from school anyway, so I’ll handle it then. Just make sure the paella price stays at 18.50 and the wine order is sent. Thanks.

content.text: Understood. The paella price is locked at 18.50 for this week. The wine order to Bodegas Turia has been sent. I will send you a reminder about the document for Abogada Torres on Monday. Have a good shift, Mateo.
